ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the rectangular coil rotates through the rotating shaft OO'; OO' is a vertical dashed axis; the external circuit has a resistor R connected at the bottom. In the figure, crosses are used to indicate that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface inward, and the crosses are mainly distributed in the right half region of the coil, with no magnetic field on the left half, so according to the figure only half of the total area of the coil is in the magnetic field, and the effective area is taken as S_eff = S/2. Then reason and calculate: the maximum value of the induced electromotive force of the AC generator is E_m = n B S_eff ω = nB(S/2)ω. Substituting n=10, B=2/π T, S=0.2 m^2, ω=10π rad/s, gives E_m = 10 × (2/π) × 0.1 × 10π = 20 V. The effective value of the sinusoidal alternating current is E = E_m/√2 = 10√2 V. The internal resistance of the coil r=2 Ω and the external resistor R=18 Ω are in series, and the total resistance R+r=20 Ω, so the effective value of the current is I = E/(R+r) = 10√2/20 = √2/2 A. The average power consumed on resistor R is P_R = I^2R = (√2/2)^2 × 18 = 9 W.

First describe the image: in the figure, the rectangular coil rotates through the rotating shaft OO'; OO' is a vertical dashed axis; the external circuit has a resistor R connected at the bottom. In the figure, crosses are used to indicate that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface inward, and the crosses are mainly distributed in the right half region of the coil, with no magnetic field on the left half, so according to the figure only half of the total area of the coil is in the magnetic field, and the effective area is taken as S_eff = S/2.

Then reason and calculate: the maximum value of the induced electromotive force of the AC generator is E_m = n B S_eff ω = nB(S/2)ω. Substituting n=10, B=2/π T, S=0.2 m^2, ω=10π rad/s, gives E_m = 10 × (2/π) × 0.1 × 10π = 20 V. The effective value of the sinusoidal alternating current is E = E_m/√2 = 10√2 V. The internal resistance of the coil r=2 Ω and the external resistor R=18 Ω are in series, and the total resistance R+r=20 Ω, so the effective value of the current is I = E/(R+r) = 10√2/20 = √2/2 A. The average power consumed on resistor R is P_R = I^2R = (√2/2)^2 × 18 = 9 W.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the number of turns of the rectangular coil of an AC generator is n=10, its resistance is r=2 Ω, and its area is $S=0.2\mathbf{m}^{2}$. In a uniform magnetic field with magnetic induction intensity $B=\frac{2}{\pi}$ T, if the coil starts from the neutral-plane position and rotates uniformly about the symmetric axis OO' perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic field with angular velocity $\omega=10\pi$ rad/s, supplying power to a resistor of $R=18\Omega$. How much electric power is consumed on resistor R?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer: The electric power consumed on resistor R is 9 W
